tagline: Four glowing monoliths ring a quiet sanctum: strike their notes in the one right order to unseal the altar.
overview:
Echo Chambers is a tiny first-person sequence puzzle, one of a set of quick minigames built to test RedEngine. You start on a white altar in the middle of a square violet chamber. Four tall monoliths stand around you, one on each side: teal, magenta, yellow and orange.

Walk to the floor just in front of a monolith to strike its note. Strike all four in the right order and the altar unseals; step back onto it to win. A wrong note simply does not count. Be aware that the game never tells you the order: it is teal, then magenta, then yellow, then orange (see Rules).
story: An ancient sanctum is sealed by harmony. A wandering monk finds four monoliths still humming around an empty altar; only someone who sounds them in the order of the old song can open the altar at the chamber's heart.
goal: Strike the four monoliths in order (teal, magenta, yellow, orange), then step onto the white altar: VICTORY. There is no way to lose.
rules: Walk onto the floor in front of a monolith (within about two metres of it) to strike its note.
The order is fixed: teal (the one you face at the start), then magenta (behind you at the start), then yellow, then orange.
A monolith struck out of order does nothing; SEQ_STEP at the top left counts the notes you have right so far.
After the fourth note SEALED drops to 0. Step back onto the altar in the middle to win.

tips: Teal, magenta, yellow, orange: the whole puzzle is knowing the order.
You do not need to touch the monolith; stepping onto the floor in front of it is enough.
ROUND, the bat and the health bar on screen belong to the engine's default player and do nothing here.

Echo Chambers is one of ten small minigames added to RedEngineGames in a single commit on 2026-09-30 ("Add 10 unique data-driven minigames with feedback and launcher support"). They were built by an AI at the owner's request, as experiments that tested RedEngine side by side with a sister engine (each game's FEEDBACK.md compares the two), but the prompt that asked for them was given in a session that is not saved on this machine.
